experiment_spec.objective: Use a common customer-qualified usable magnet target and deadline; show the cost versus unmet/late demand frontier.
common_inputs: Grade, geometry, tolerance, coating and temperature/demagnetization performance
Annual accepted tonnes or part count, deadline and budget
Identical initial inventories, supplier qualifications, allocations and contracts; separate the true cold-start case
alternatives: Domestic capacity with domestic or imported equipment
Qualified allied finished-magnet imports and multiple sourcing
A stock bridge with grade, shelf-life and traceability constraints
lifecycle_cost_components: Machine quote, engineering, integration, buildings, utilities and permits
Shipment, insurance, confirmed duties, installation, FAT/SAT and training
Feedstock, yield loss, rework, scrap, energy, inert gas and consumables
Maintenance, spare parts, service visits, outages and backup capacity
Qualification/test lots, tooling, working capital and carrying inventory
Replacement/decommissioning and residual value where relevant
experiment_spec.capacity_method: Solve stage flows after correct mass-basis conversions, with stage yields, operating availability, ramp and customer acceptance. The bottleneck constrains accepted output; incompatible units cannot be multiplied or summed.
switching_conditions: A domestic line cannot meet a deadline before construction, commissioning, ramp and qualification finish; qualified imports/stock must bridge that interval.
Imports or multiple sourcing are preferable when their delivered lifecycle premium is below avoided late/unmet-demand loss plus capital and service costs within the shared budget.
Redundancy or extra service becomes valuable when avoided outage/qualification losses exceed its cost; shared upstream feed or spares dependencies remain.
Extra casting capacity reduces unmet demand only when feed, metal conversion, powder, tooling, coating, testing and customer approval also clear.
sensitivity_axes: Qualified import allocation, lead time and export disruption
Quoted freight/insurance, verified tariff layers and FX
Deadline, budget and consequences of unmet/late demand
experiment_spec.country_price_hypothesis: Untested: no matched specification, delivery, acceptance and service comparison of China/Japan/U.S. quotations verified. Do not use uniform country cost multipliers.
experiment_spec.calibration_boundary: Project capex and nameplate are context anchors, not machine quotes or a national U.S. investment total. Preserve illustrative capital credits until coherent quotes and operating data exist.
